cve_summary: Multiple race conditions in the Web Audio implementation in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 30.0.1599.66, allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via vectors related to threading in core/html/HTMLMediaElement.cpp, core/platform/audio/AudioDSPKernelProcessor.cpp, core/platform/audio/HRTFElevation.cpp, and modules/webaudio/ConvolverNode.cpp.
commit_message:
Fix threading races on ConvolverNode::m_reverb in ConvolverNode::latencyFrames()

According to the crash report (https://cluster-fuzz.appspot.com/testcase?key=6515787040817152),
ConvolverNode::m_reverb races between ConvolverNode::latencyFrames() and ConvolverNode::setBuffer().
This CL adds a proper lock for ConvolverNode::m_reverb.

BUG=223962
No tests because the crash depends on threading races and thus not reproducible.

Review URL: https://chromiumcodereview.appspot.com/23514037

docstring:
Summary: This code defines the `ConvolverNode` class, which processes audio signals using convolution with an impulse response in a web audio context.

Parameters: 
N/A

Returns: 
N/A

Logic: The `ConvolverNode` class inherits from `AudioNode` and initializes with a specified audio context and sample rate. It manages audio processing through a reverb engine, which is created from an audio buffer containing the impulse response. The `process` method handles audio frames, ensuring synchronization with potential changes to the impulse response using a mutex. If the node is not initialized or the reverb is not set, it outputs silence. The `setBuffer` method validates the audio buffer and wraps it in an `AudioBus`, which is then used to create the reverb. The class also provides methods to retrieve the audio buffer and calculate tail and latency times, returning large values when locks cannot be acquired to avoid blocking the audio processing thread.
